arxiv-2102-09457.title: K-stability and Fujita approximation
arxiv-2102-09457.creator: Chi Li
arxiv-2102-09457.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chi Li. This note is a continuation to the paper [ 26 ] . We derive a formula for non-Archimedean Monge-Ampère measures of big models. As applications, we derive a positive intersection formula for non-Archimedean Mabuchi functional, and further reduces the ( Aut ​ ( X , L ) 0 {\rm Aut}(X,L)_{0} )-uniform Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture for polarized manifolds to a conjecture on the existence of approximate Zariski decompositions that satisfy some asymptotic vanishing condition.

arxiv-2201-04911.title: Strong [OIII] λ ​ 5007 \lambda 5007 emission line compact galaxies in LAMOST DR9: Blueberries, Green Peas and Purple Grapes
arxiv-2201-04911.creator: Siqi Liu, A-Li Luo ∗, Huan Yang, Shi-Yin Shen, Jun-Xian Wang, Hao-Tong Zhang, Zhenya Zheng, Yi-Han Song, Xiao Kong, Jian-Ling Wang, Jian-Jun Chen
arxiv-2201-04911.description: Abstract Green Pea and Blueberry galaxies are well-known for their compact size, low mass, strong emission lines and analogs to high- z z Ly α \alpha emitting galaxies. In this study, 1547 strong [OIII] λ ​ 5007 \lambda 5007 emission line compact galaxies with 1694 spectra are selected from LAMOST DR9 at the redshift range from 0.0 to 0.59.

arxiv-2205-15823.title: Predicting non-native speech perception using the Perceptual Assimilation Model and state-of-the-art acoustic models
arxiv-2205-15823.creator: Juliette Millet, Ioana Chitoran, Ewan Dunbar
arxiv-2205-15823.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Juliette Millet, Ioana Chitoran, Ewan Dunbar. Our native language influences the way we perceive speech sounds, affecting our ability to discriminate non-native sounds. We compare two ideas about the influence of the native language on speech perception: the Perceptual Assimilation Model, which appeals to a mental classification of sounds into native phoneme categories, versus the idea that rich, fine-grained phonetic representations tuned to the statistics of the native language, are sufficient.

arxiv-2206-10892.title: I 2 I^{2} R-Net: Intra- and Inter-Human Relation Network for Multi-Person Pose Estimation
arxiv-2206-10892.creator: Yiwei Ding, Wenjin Deng, Yinglin Zheng, Pengfei Liu, Meihong Wang, Xuan Cheng, Jianmin Bao, Dong Chen, Ming Zeng
arxiv-2206-10892.description: Abstract In this paper, we present the Intra- and Inter-Human Relation Networks ( I 2 I^{2} R-Net ) for Multi-Person Pose Estimation. It involves two basic modules. First, the Intra-Human Relation Module operates on a single person and aims to capture Intra-Human dependencies. Second, the Inter-Human Relation Module considers the relation between multiple instances and focuses on capturing Inter-Human interactions.

arxiv-2207-00401.title: Autonomous Intraluminal Navigation of a Soft Robot using Deep-Learning-based Visual Servoing
arxiv-2207-00401.creator: Jorge F. Lazo † \dagger, Chun-Feng Lai † \dagger, Sara Moccia, Benoit Rosa, Michele Catellani, Michel de Mathelin, Giancarlo Ferrigno, Paul Breedveld, Jenny Dankelman, Elena De Momi
arxiv-2207-00401.description: Abstract Navigation inside luminal organs is an arduous task that requires non-intuitive coordination between the movement of the operator’s hand and the information obtained from the endoscopic video. The development of tools to automate certain tasks could alleviate the physical and mental load of doctors during interventions, allowing them to focus on diagnosis and decision-making tasks.

arxiv-2307-08404.title: Influence of the Commutator Properties of Hamiltonians on the Robustness of Quantum Circuits
arxiv-2307-08404.creator: Vitalii Slynko, Vladyslav Bivziuk
arxiv-2307-08404.description: Abstract We have proved new estimates for the coherent control errors of quantum circuits used in quantum computing. These estimates essentially take into account the commutator properties of the Hamiltonians and are based on the formulas of the commutator calculus.

arxiv-2309-07704.title: NutritionVerse: Empirical Study of Various Dietary Intake Estimation Approaches
arxiv-2309-07704.creator: Chi-en Amy Tai, Matthew Keller, Saeejith Nair, Yuhao Chen, Yifan Wu, Olivia Markham, Krish Parmar, Pengcheng Xi, Heather Keller, Sharon Kirkpatrick, Alexander Wong
arxiv-2309-07704.description: Abstract Accurate dietary intake estimation is critical for informing policies and programs to support healthy eating, as malnutrition has been directly linked to decreased quality of life. However self-reporting methods such as food diaries suffer from substantial bias. Other conventional dietary assessment techniques and emerging alternative approaches such as mobile applications incur high time costs and may necessitate trained personnel.

arxiv-2402-19457.title: COSMIC : Mutual Information for Task-Agnostic Summarization Evaluation
arxiv-2402-19457.creator: Maxime Darrin, Philippe Formont, Jackie Chi Kit Cheung, Pablo Piantanida
arxiv-2402-19457.description: Abstract Assessing the quality of summarizers poses significant challenges—gold summaries are hard to obtain and their suitability depends on the use context of the summarization system. Who is the user of the system, and what do they intend to do with the summary?

arxiv-2507-03151.title: Complexity of learning matchings and half graphs via edge queries
arxiv-2507-03151.creator: Nikhil S. Mande, Swagato Sanyal, Viktor Zamaraev
arxiv-2507-03151.description: Abstract The problem of learning or reconstructing an unknown graph from a known family via partial-information queries arises as a mathematical model in various contexts. The most basic type of access to the graph is via edge queries , where an algorithm may query the presence/absence of an edge between a pair of vertices of its choosing, at unit cost.

arxiv-2509-23340.title: CrediBench: Building Web-Scale Network Datasets for Information Integrity Equal Contribution.
arxiv-2509-23340.creator: Emma Kondrup † {\dagger}, Sebastian Sabry † {\dagger}, Hussein Abdallah † {\dagger}, Zachary Yang † {\dagger}, James Zhou, Kellin Pelrine, Jean-François Godbout, Michael Bronstein, Reihaneh Rabbany, Shenyang Huang † {\dagger}
arxiv-2509-23340.description: Abstract Online misinformation poses an escalating threat, amplified by the Internet’s open nature and increasingly capable LLMs that generate persuasive yet deceptive content. Existing misinformation detection methods typically focus on either textual content or network structure in isolation, failing to leverage the rich, dynamic interplay between website content and hyperlink relationships that characterizes real-world misinformation ecosystems.

arxiv-2601-12314.title: A Similarity Network for Correlating Musical Structure to Military Strategy
arxiv-2601-12314.creator: Yiwen Zhang, Hui Zhang, Fanqin Meng
arxiv-2601-12314.description: Abstract Music perception, a multi-sensory process based on the synesthesia effect, is an essential component of music aesthetic education. Understanding music structure helps both perception and aesthetic education. Music structure incorporates a range of information, the coordination of which forms the melody, just as different military actions cooperate to produce a military strategy.

arxiv-2602-07614.title: Knowledge Graphs-Driven Intelligence for Distributed Decision Systems Conference: 2025 IEEE/ACM 18th International Conference on Utility and Cloud Computing; December 1–4, 2025; France, France 2025 IEEE/ACM 18th International Conference on Utility and Cloud Computing (UCC ’25), December 1–4, 2025, F
arxiv-2602-07614.creator: Rosario Napoli, Gabriele Morabito, Antonio Celesti, Massimo Villari, Maria Fazio
arxiv-2602-07614.description: Abstract . Modern distributed decision-making systems face significant challenges arising from data heterogeneity, dynamic environments, and the need for decentralized coordination. This paper introduces the Knowledge Sharing paradigm as an innovative approach that uses the semantic richness of Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and the representational power of Graph Embeddings (GEs) to achieve decentralized intelligence.

pmc-10582287.title: Anton syndrome with bilateral occipital infarct: A case report
pmc-10582287.creator: Dylan Mankoo
pmc-10582287.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Anton syndrome results from damage to the visual cortex of the occipital lobes, where the anterior visual pathways remain intact. This damage results in the characteristic triad of cortical blindness, visual anosognosia, and visual confabulation. This case describes an 80-year-old male with a background of renal transplant 7 years prior, admitted to hospital with worsening transplant function, and soon after developed sudden onset cortical blindness.

pmc-11474550.title: Insights Into Gastrointestinal Motility Through the Use of Optogenetic Sensors
pmc-11474550.creator: Jing Wang, Jun Xiao
pmc-11474550.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The authors employed an inducible Cre-loxP recombination system to generate mice expressing channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2) in ICC and confirmed expression through genotyping and immunofluorescence analysis. Using such a model, the authors investigated the effects of light stimulation on colonic muscle strips specifically in ICC and demonstrated that 470 nm blue light could induce premature low-frequency and high-amplitude (LFHA) contractions while isometric force was present. Furthermore, this LFHA activity was inhibited by T16Ainh-A01, a specific antagonist of the anoctamin 1 channel in ICC.

pmc-11504037.title: Current Perspectives on Olfactory Loss in Atypical Parkinsonisms—A Review Article
pmc-11504037.creator: Katarzyna Bochniak, Mateusz Soszyński, Natalia Madetko-Alster, Piotr Alster, Eun-Young Lee
pmc-11504037.description: Introduction: Atypical parkinsonisms (APs) present various symptoms including motor impairment, cognitive decline, and autonomic dysfunction. Olfactory loss (OL), being a significant non-motor symptom, has emerged as an under-evaluated, yet potentially valuable, feature that might aid in the differential diagnosis of APs. State of the art: The most pronounced OL is usually associated with Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB).

pmc-12567767.title: Implementation of an SS-Compensated LC-Thermistor Topology for Passive Wireless Temperature Sensing
pmc-12567767.creator: Seyit Ahmet Sis, Yeliz Dikerler Kozar
pmc-12567767.description: Highlights What are the main findings? A passive wireless temperature sensor is implemented using SS-compensated magnetically coupled LC tanks.The thermistor’s resistance is directly reflected in the input impedance at split resonance frequencies. What is the implication of the main finding? Enables accurate, battery-free, and contactless temperature sensing through impedance monitoring.Suitable for applications requiring simple and reliable wireless sensing topologies.

pmc-12661258.title: Hippocampal Subregion Function and Its Clinical Correlations in Childhood Autism Spectrum Disorders
pmc-12661258.creator: Hui‐Xian Li, De‐Sheng Xuan, Ronghao Mu, Chi Qin, Xin Zhao
pmc-12661258.description: The hippocampus plays a crucial role in memory and social processing, both of which are impaired in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Investigating the functional activity of hippocampal subregions can provide valuable insights into their involvement in ASD‐related social and behavioral symptoms.

pmc-12707208.title: Optimizing reference gene selection for accurate gene expression analysis in plants
pmc-12707208.creator: Zili Xiong, Cunnian Fu, Shaoyong Huang, Jianlei Shi
pmc-12707208.description: Accurate selection of reference genes is crucial for reliable gene expression analysis in plants. Traditional reference genes, such as GAPDH and ACT, are widely used but often show variable stability under different conditions, stresses, tissue types, and developmental stages. Recent advances in multi-omics technologies, including transcriptomics, offer new approaches for improving reference gene selection.

pmc-13246649.title: The immune-cardiovascular metabolic circuitry in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury: from metabolic signal release to spatiotemporal reprogramming
pmc-13246649.creator: Conghao Tan, Junjie Zhou, Jiawen Li, Xinyi Zhang, Wei Yuan
pmc-13246649.description: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) remains a major driver of infarct expansion, adverse remodeling, and poor outcomes after reperfusion therapy, yet mechanism-based treatments remain limited. Emerging evidence suggests that MIRI is not simply the additive result of oxidative stress and sterile inflammation. Rather, it reflects a spatiotemporally organized imbalance in immune–cardiac metabolic communication.

pmc-13559473.title: Comparison of in‐field secondary cancer risk based on therapeutic proton dose between proton arc therapy and intensity‐modulated proton therapy in lung cancer patients
pmc-13559473.creator: Yuankang Xu, Wenguang Chen, Junxiang Wu, Hao Guo, Fanrui Zeng, Tianyu Zhang, Feng Yang, Xinhui Huang, Da Zhang, Xianliang Wang
pmc-13559473.description: BackgroundProton arc therapy (PAT) is an emerging delivery modality that delivers proton beams through continuous gantry rotation combined with spot scanning. Compared with intensity‐modulated proton therapy (IMPT), PAT improves target conformity and spares organs at risk. However, the dynamic multi‐angle irradiation pattern may alter the low‐dose region distribution: the low‐dose bath expands while the integral dose decreases.
